1. Model tends to overestimate prices in the early part of the forecast horizon, especially after recent spikes — reduce initial forecast values by 1–3% to align with observed mean reversion.

2. Model consistently underestimates the true price in the final 5–7 days of the forecast — increase the last 5–7 forecast values by 1–2% to match observed upward bias.

3. After a sharp price spike (e.g., >65), model often overshoots in the next 3–5 days — apply a “cool-down” correction: reduce forecast by 2–5% for the following 3–5 days.

4. Model exhibits persistent bias toward higher values in the middle of the forecast — apply a “midpoint correction”: subtract 1–2% from forecast values at positions 15–25 (index 15–25 of 30-day forecast).

5. Model fails to capture mean reversion after strong upward moves — if true outcome shows a 5–10% drop from peak, reduce forecast by 1–3% for the next 3–5 days to reflect expected reversion.

6. Model often overreacts to recent low prices — if history shows a recent dip, avoid sharp upward forecasts; instead, use a “low-rebound” heuristic: forecast = previous 3-day average + 1–2% adjustment.
